articles.title: Sepia
articles.summary: Flat satin panel with a soft dusty haze and no sparkle, like faded old paint, in whatever colour you give it. Reads as plain satin paint in whatever colour you give it, slightly low in metal, nothing to see; a calm faded look.
articles.what: Up close: The paint is a flat colour with no pattern. The spec strip shows a soft cloudy mottle, but it is a contrast-stretched view of a tiny variation (roughness std 2, metal and clearcoat flat), so on the car it is a smooth even satin with only a faint dusty haze. From a distance: Reads as plain satin paint in whatever colour you give it, slightly low in metal, nothing to see; a calm faded look. Measured spec (average): metal 60, roughness 77, coat 40. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: stock car, dirt late model, show car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Sepia on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body panels everywhere: even base
Hood, roof and sides take stripes and graphics well
Numbers read cleanly on a flat even surface in any colour with contrast.
Any pattern: it is a quiet base; stripes, camo or graphics all sit on it cleanly
Pairs well with: cream, brown, chrome.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a sepia colour: the name suggests brown, but it takes the colour you give it; the red in the data is a placeholder, the lit render is flat grey
Not a visible mottled pattern: the cloud map is almost flat in the numbers
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to high-gloss finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 60 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 77 (satin gloss), clearcoat 40 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to high-gloss finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any pattern: it is a quiet base; stripes, camo or graphics all sit on it cleanly; flat colour graphics and plates
Patterns to avoid: none; just avoid heavy gloss patterns that fight the faded feel
Spec overlays that work: grain, flake or brushed spec patterns: it has almost no texture so they stand out; a light hazy spec for extra age
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.what: Up close: Soft glowing blotches, 10-25 px, in lime yellow-green over a dull grey-olive ground, packed like a swarm of fuzzy firefly lights, with a fine grain of speckle running through everything. The glows are blurred, never sharp points. From a distance: Reads as a muddy olive with a lime-green glowing mottle; the blotches merge into a hazy light-green cloudy shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 113, roughness 179, coat 94. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Firefly" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: broad panels where the glow clouds read
All-over field, no seam visible
White or black numbers with an outline read; green and yellow numbers sink into the glows.
Large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the soft glow stays behind them
Pairs well with: black, chrome, white, deep purple.
pitfalls: Not crisp glitter pieces: the glows are blurry blobs
Not a bright neon green: the ground is dull and the lime only shows in the blobs
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to another flake finish.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 113 (pearl-level metal), roughness 179 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 94 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to another flake finish.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the soft glow stays behind them; soft fades or clouds: the blotches show through
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter, speckle or static patterns: pile into noise; other sparkle or flake finishes
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sheen: makes the glows pop; none needed
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Spectral
articles.summary: Near-black satin with faint blue oval glows and subtle iridescent shimmer, very dark and quiet. Reads as a very dark navy with three dim glowing circles, barely there; the car looks blacked out, with a faint teal-blue haze.
articles.what: Up close: Near-black navy ground with a very fine tooth of tiny pale dashes, and three large oval outlines in teal-blue, about 100 to 190 px tall, each with a soft grey-blue glow inside that is brighter at the bottom. The ovals touch at the edges, like three eyes or lenses. From a distance: Reads as a very dark navy with three dim glowing circles, barely there; the car looks blacked out, with a faint teal-blue haze. Measured spec (average): metal 29, roughness 74, coat 45. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Spectral on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood or roof: the three ovals land near the centre as a faint accent
Side panels: the group appears once on the door, check the preview
White, silver or yellow numbers read strongly; dark numbers vanish.
Almost any: it is a very dark quiet base; bright stripes and graphics read strongly
Pairs well with: chrome, white, electric blue, silver.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not an even dark satin: the old card says faint oval glows, which is correct, but the outlines are crisp teal rings, more than a glow
Not iridescent in the picture: colours are only navy and teal, the shimmer is claimed
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, low-contrast numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 29 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 74 (satin gloss), clearcoat 45 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, low-contrast numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost any: it is a very dark quiet base; bright stripes and graphics read strongly; flat colour graphics and plates
Patterns to avoid: other oval, eye or bubble patterns; busy centre patterns that hide the ovals
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat spec for a deeper black; a metallic flake spec, since this has little metal
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Stained Glass
articles.summary: Smooth high-gloss surface with broad soft colour shifts, like light through thick coloured glass; almost no sparkle, deep wet-looking panels. Reads as a clean deep high-gloss version of whatever colour you pick, with a very slight watery unevenness in the reflections; nothing like a window.
articles.what: Up close: The paint is a flat placeholder grey, so it takes your colour. The only structure is in the spec: faint broad vertical smudges of metal and roughness, a few soft bright blobs, no cells, no leading lines. Real variation is tiny (metal std 11, roughness std 7, clearcoat fixed at max gloss). From a distance: Reads as a clean deep high-gloss version of whatever colour you pick, with a very slight watery unevenness in the reflections; nothing like a window. Measured spec (average): metal 34, roughness 24, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Stained Glass on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: big smooth areas show the reflection
Skip small trim: nothing to see
Numbers stay perfectly readable; there is no texture under them.
Fine flake or micro-pattern: the base is smooth enough that any grain reads clearly
Pairs well with: chrome, gold, black, white.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a stained-glass window pattern: the render shows no panes, lead lines or multiple colours, only smooth gloss
Not red: the red palette entry is misleading, the colour is whatever you apply
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 34 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 24 (wet mirror gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine flake or micro-pattern: the base is smooth enough that any grain reads clearly; hex or Voronoi cell overlays: they add the stained-glass leading the finish itself lacks
Patterns to avoid: heavy camo or weave: kills the glossy depth; coarse noise: fights the soft broad variation
Spec overlays that work: cell or crackle spec lines: gives dark came-like seams; pearl or fine sparkle spec for shimmering glass
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Stucco
articles.summary: Flat chalky plaster surface, faintly grainy and dry, with a soft semi-matte sheen; looks like painted wall render rather than car paint. Reads as your plain colour in a dull semi-matte, slightly chalky; the mottle is not visible at distance.
articles.what: Up close: Takes your colour. The paint is a flat colour; the texture is only in the spec, a soft blotchy plaster grain with 20-40 px mottles. Roughness varies only a few points (R 162, std 5) and metal and clearcoat are flat, so the effect is a very faint dry, chalky mottle. From a distance: Reads as your plain colour in a dull semi-matte, slightly chalky; the mottle is not visible at distance. Measured spec (average): metal 40, roughness 162, coat 220. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Stucco on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body panels, bumpers and trim: works as a plain dry base
Hood and roof: broad flat panels carry the faint mottle best
Numbers read fine; there is no texture to disturb them, just use contrast against your colour.
Fine grain or sand patterns: adds the visible plaster texture the base lacks
Pairs well with: matte black, brown, olive, white.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a visible textured paint: the colour is flat, the texture is almost spec only
Not a rough sandpaper grain: mottles are broad and soft
Avoid: numbers over heavy texture, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 40 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 162 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 220 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Matte reads as flat colour, so a clean saturated colour looks richer than a muddy mid-grey; pair it with a gloss or metal neighbour for contrast. Avoid: numbers over heavy texture, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine grain or sand patterns: adds the visible plaster texture the base lacks; cracked or crackle patterns: pushes it toward old wall render
Patterns to avoid: gloss or glitter patterns: fights the chalky dry feel; bold geometric: a rough plaster surface does not suit crisp shapes
Spec overlays that work: grain or pebble spec overlay: makes the roughness variation visible; matte-to-satin mottle spec for stronger plaster feel
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
